name: Analyze customer feedback from Zendesk and Gong with Claude and report in Notion

parameters.content:
## Analyze customer feedback from Zendesk and Gong with Claude and report in Notion

Product and success teams that read tickets one at a time and miss the pattern.

### How it works
Trigger: Daily pulls from each source; the weekly report compiles Monday morning.
1. Collect feedback
2. Classify by theme and sentiment
3. Extract the quotable line
4. Aggregate
5. Write the weekly report
6. Route urgent items
7. Deliver and store
8. Maintain the taxonomy
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items.

### Setup
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials: Anthropic, plus Zendesk / Intercom / Gong, Notion + Google Sheets.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

### Customization tips
Set the theme taxonomy and the report cadence in the Config node; add Intercom or survey tools as sources.
Guardrail to keep: Personal data is stripped from quotes; sources are linked, not reproduced.

Full blueprint: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/customer-feedback-analysis/

## Trigger and config
The entry point and the one node you edit: names, approver, quiet hours, test mode.

## 1. Collect feedback
Survey responses (Typeform, Delighted, Qualtrics), reviews (G2, app stores, Trustpilot), support tickets (Zendesk, Intercom), call notes (Gong, Fireflies), and social mentions, each with source, customer segment and date

## 2. Classify by theme and sentiment
Each item tagged with one or more themes from your taxonomy (pricing, onboarding, reliability, feature X…) and a sentiment; items that fit no theme are collected as candidates for a new one

## 3. Extract the quotable line
The sentence that carries the feedback, cleaned of personal data, kept with a link to the source record

## 4. Aggregate
Volume and sentiment per theme per week, by segment and plan; trend versus the previous eight weeks; new-theme candidates ranked by frequency

## 5. Write the weekly report
Top themes with numbers and quotes, rising and falling themes, new themes to review, and — clearly separated as inference — what the pattern suggests

## 6. Route urgent items

## 7. Deliver and store
Report posted to Slack and stored in the wiki; the classified dataset available for product to query

## 8. Maintain the taxonomy
Themes and definitions live in a sheet product owns; new-theme candidates are approved there and the classifier picks them up next run

Every later node reads these values. Keep test_mode on for the first week.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Write the weekly report" step of the Customer Feedback Analysis Automation workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Top themes with numbers and quotes, rising and falling themes, new themes to review, and — clearly separated as inference — what the pattern suggests. Every claim cites a count or a quote.

Rules:
- Personal data is stripped from quotes; sources are linked, not reproduced.
- The taxonomy is owned by product; the agent proposes new themes, it does not create them.
- Inference is labelled as inference and separated from counts and quotes.
- Spike alerts require a minimum volume to avoid false alarms from single items.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.
